Proxy-Cheap is the budget replacement for NetNut: rotating residential is currently advertised at $0.78/GB with no monthly plan, static ISP proxies cost a few dollars per IP per month, and SOCKS5 with UDP is supported. That covers the two products most NetNut customers used. The trade-offs are thinner targeting on rotating traffic (country and ISP rather than city) and less independent benchmark data, so it fits easy-to-moderate targets best. Teams that relied on NetNut's US city targeting should test carefully or consider a mid-market alternative.

Former NetNut customers searching for Proxy-Cheap are usually looking for the cheapest safe landing spot. NetNut's domains were seized by the FBI on July 2, 2026, after Google tied its residential network to the Popa botnet. Proxy-Cheap sells many of the same product types, including static residential (ISP) proxies, rotating residential, mobile and datacenter IPs, at prices well below NetNut's old rates. This page compares them and explains how to switch.
What happened to NetNut?

NetNut stopped being a normal buying option on July 2, 2026. That day the FBI and IRS Criminal Investigation seized NetNut-related domains, and Google published research linking the network's residential exit nodes to the Popa botnet, which it estimated at two million or more hijacked home devices. NetNut's parent, Alarum Technologies, rejects the allegations, but its main domains went on to show seizure banners and its share price fell sharply. Whatever the final legal outcome, routing business traffic through that infrastructure now carries legal and reputational risk.

blocks.text: Proxy-Cheap in 2026: what you get

Proxy-Cheap has sold proxies since 2018 and says it serves 45,000+ customers. It offers seven product types: static residential (ISP) in IPv4 and IPv6, rotating residential, datacenter IPv4 and IPv6, and static and rotating mobile. Rotating residential is pure pay-as-you-go with no monthly plan, and the site claims coverage in 180+ countries. Targeting is mainly country and ISP level, and all products support SOCKS5 including UDP. It is a strong value pick, though independent benchmarks of its rotating pool have been mixed.

Proxy-Cheap lives up to its name: rotating residential traffic is currently advertised at $0.78/GB (70% off a $2.60 list price) with no subscription, and static ISP and datacenter IPs cost a dollar or two per month. The catalog is broad, covering IPv6 options few competitors offer, and payment by card, PayPal, Alipay or crypto is easy. The trade-offs are thinner targeting (country and ISP rather than city on rotating residential) and less published performance data than the bigger brands.

Strengths: Very low per-GB price while the promotion runs; No monthly commitment on rotating residential; Broad catalog including IPv6 and static mobile; SOCKS5 with UDP support. Weak spots: Targeting is mostly country and ISP, not city; Residential pool size not separately published; Mixed results in some independent benchmarks.
What NetNut offered, and how Proxy-Cheap compares

Before the seizure, NetNut was best known for ISP-sourced static residential proxies and a fast rotating residential network aimed at scraping, ad verification and brand-protection teams. Its residential rates generally ran from about $1.87 to $3.53 per GB on larger plans, with higher effective prices on entry plans. Proxy-Cheap covers much of the same ground: static residential (ipv4 and ipv6), datacenter ipv4/ipv6, static and rotating mobile sit alongside its residential network, which advertises Not separately published (155M+ claimed across all products) IPs in 180+ countries.

Most NetNut accounts were built around three things: static ISP IPs for long-lived sessions, rotating residential traffic with US state and city targeting, and high concurrency for scraping. On static ISP-style IPs, Proxy-Cheap's answer is yes; its other products are static residential (IPv4 and IPv6), datacenter IPv4/IPv6, static and rotating mobile. On billing, Proxy-Cheap uses pay-as-you-go per GB; static products billed per IP per month, and unused traffic is handled as follows: pay-as-you-go balance, no monthly commitment. Map each of your old NetNut zones to one of these before you migrate, so nothing breaks on the day you switch.

Proxy-Cheap's rotating residential proxies are pay-as-you-go, currently listed from $0.78/GB (a promotional price against a $2.60/GB list rate). Static residential ISP proxies start around $2.44 per IP per month, datacenter IPv4 at about $1.49, datacenter IPv6 from $0.15, and rotating mobile at $5.99/GB.

Quick cost check for Proxy-Cheap: 10 GB comes to $7.80 at the promo rate ($26 at list), and 100 GB comes to $78 at the promo rate ($260 at list). NetNut's larger plans used to run about $1.87-$3.53/GB, so compare against what you actually paid rather than NetNut's headline rate.
How to migrate from NetNut to Proxy-Cheap
1. Export your NetNut usage history and list the countries, cities and session types you actually used, so you can map them to Proxy-Cheap's targeting (country and ISP).

2. Test before you commit. Proxy-Cheap's testing option: 7-day $1.99 trial on static residential and datacenter IPs. Run your real targets for a day on the smallest purchase before moving production traffic.
3. Swap the gateway host and credentials in your scraper or browser profiles. Proxy-Cheap supports HTTP, HTTPS, SOCKS5 (TCP and UDP).
4. Compare success rate, response time and cost per successful request against your old NetNut baseline, then move traffic over in stages.
5. Remove any NetNut SDKs, browser extensions or endpoints from your systems, and rotate any credentials that were stored alongside them.
Where Proxy-Cheap fits best
General web scraping: workable. Why: cheap traffic, though independent benchmark results have been mixed.
SERP and rank tracking: workable. Why: workable for light rank tracking at a low cost.
Social media and multi-account management: strong fit. Why: cheap static ISP and mobile IPs for persistent identities.
E-commerce price and stock monitoring: workable. Why: fine for country-level price checks.
Ad verification and geo-testing: weak fit. Why: lacks city-level targeting on rotating residential.
Tight budgets: strong fit. Why: the lowest advertised per-GB price in this pairing.
Protocols and sessions

Proxy-Cheap supports HTTP, HTTPS, SOCKS5 (TCP and UDP) and offers rotating and sticky sessions. Targeting covers country and ISP across 180+ countries. Like NetNut's residential gateway, it works through a single backconnect endpoint with location and session options passed in the username, plus IP whitelisting.
How to vet a residential proxy provider after NetNut

The NetNut case showed that a residential pool can look like a normal enterprise product while resting on devices whose owners never meaningfully agreed to share their connection. Before you move traffic to any provider, including Proxy-Cheap, ask a few direct questions and keep the answers on file:
How are residential IPs sourced? Look for an opt-in SDK or app programme with clear user
consent and compensation, and ask which partner apps are involved.
Does the provider publish an ethics or sourcing policy, and has it been audited or certified (for
example AppEsteem or ISO 27001)?
What KYC does the provider apply to customers, and which target categories are restricted?
Strict onboarding is a good sign, not an inconvenience.
How does it handle abuse reports, and is there a named legal entity and jurisdiction behind the
service?
Can you get contractual assurances, such as a data-processing agreement, if your compliance
team needs them?
Bottom line

NetNut is no longer a provider you can plan around, so the real decision is which network replaces it. Proxy-Cheap is strongest for price-sensitive scraping at moderate difficulty and buyers who want static ISP or IPv6 IPs cheaply, starts at $0.78/GB promotional price (list $2.60/GB), and offers 7-day $1.99 trial on static residential and datacenter IPs.
